questions.explain: The classifier assigns each query to OLTP_SHORT, ANALYTICAL, BATCH_ETL, or MIXED_ADHOC using features from Query Store (duration, CPU, reads/writes, write ratio, execution regularity) so the router knows whether and where it can move.
options: To predict which queries will fail with syntax errors
To assign each query to a routing class (OLTP_SHORT, ANALYTICAL, BATCH_ETL, MIXED_ADHOC) from its Query Store execution signature
To generate index recommendations for each query
To estimate the dollar cost of each query execution
questions.q: What is the purpose of the ML workload classifier in the routing architecture?

questions.explain: Staleness = redo_queue_size / redo_rate (seconds behind); the router minimizes α·staleness + β·load_cpu_percent, restricted to replicas within the workload's freshness tolerance.
options: Round-robin across all secondaries
Always the secondary with the most free disk space
The replica with the lowest network latency
The secondary minimizing α·staleness_seconds + β·load_cpu_percent among replicas within the freshness tolerance
questions.q: How does the router choose among eligible secondary replicas for an ANALYTICAL query?

questions.explain: Resource Governor makes routing enforceable in the engine: the classifier maps the session's workload label to a capped workload group, so a misclassified or misbehaving query hits a resource envelope instead of starving other workloads.
options: To replace the need for readable secondaries
To enforce routing decisions inside the engine — mapping each session's workload class to a capped workload group
To encrypt connections between the router and SQL Server
To automatically rewrite queries for the secondary's schema
questions.q: What role does Resource Governor play in the intelligent routing design?

questions.explain: The primary is the safe default: uncertain classification, stale scorecards, or no fresh-enough secondary all fall back to primary routing, with every fallback logged — the design earns trust by degrading to current behavior.
options: Route to a random secondary to spread load
Queue the query until telemetry recovers
Fall back to the primary — the safe default — and log the fallback reason
Reject the connection with an error
questions.q: What is the router's fallback behavior when the classifier is uncertain or the replica scorecard is stale?

questions.explain: Shadow mode logs what the router would have decided without changing behavior; cutover happens per application (reporting first) only after shadow decisions prove better on primary CPU and freshness compliance.
options: Run the router in shadow mode first, verify its decisions beat static routing, then cut over one application at a time starting with reporting
Switch all applications to the router on day one
Disable the fallback logic to force the model to learn faster
Route everything to secondaries immediately and measure complaints
questions.q: What rollout strategy does the chapter recommend for the router service?
